ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A block of mass $m$ is dropped vertically onto a fixed ramp with an angle $\theta$. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction are represented by $\mu$. The block is dropped such that it does not rotate after colliding with the ramp. Assume the collision time is negligible. The following physical constants are provided for reference:
$g = 9.8 \, \text{N/kg}$, $G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$, $k = 8.99 \times 10^9 \, \text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2$, $k_m = 10^{-7} \, \text{T}\cdot\text{m/A}$, $c = 3.00 \times 10^8 \, \text{m/s}$, $k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{J/K}$, $N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23} \, (\text{mol})^{-1}$, $R = 8.31 \, \text{J/(mol}\cdot\text{K)}$, $\sigma = 5.67 \times 10^{-8} \, \text{J/(s}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{K}^4)$, $e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}$, $1 \, \text{eV} = 1.602 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{J}$, $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34} \, \text{J}\cdot\text{s}$, $m_e = 9.109 \times 10^{-31} \, \text{kg} = 0.511 \, \text{MeV}/c^2$.
Also, $(1+x)^n \approx 1 + nx$ for $|x| \ll 1$, $\sin \theta \approx \theta - \frac{1}{6}\theta^3$ for $|\theta| \ll 1$, $\cos \theta \approx 1 - \frac{1}{2}\theta^2$ for $|\theta| \ll 1$.
$M_\odot = 1.989 \times 10^{30} \, \text{kg}$, $L_\odot = 3.828 \times 10^{26} \, \text{W}$, $R_{\text{earth}} = 1.5 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m}$, $\lambda_{\text{max}} = 500 \, \text{nm}$.

1. Suppose the block's speed just before it hits the ramp is $v$ and the block slides down the ramp immediately after impact. What is the speed of the block right after the collision?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Resolve the block's incoming vertical speed v into components relative to the incline. The component parallel to the ramp and directed downslope is v sin(theta). The component perpendicular into the ramp is v cos(theta). Because the collision time is negligible, gravity gives negligible impulse during the collision; only the contact impulses from the ramp matter. Since the block slides down the ramp immediately after impact, kinetic friction acts during impact and is directed upslope. The normal impulse removes the incoming normal momentum, so J_N = m v cos(theta). The friction impulse has magnitude mu J_N = mu m v cos(theta), reducing the downslope momentum. Applying impulse-momentum along the slope gives m u = m v sin(theta) - mu m v cos(theta). Therefore u = v(sin(theta) - mu cos(theta)).

From the ramp angle, the initial downslope component is v sin(theta), and the component into the ramp is v cos(theta). During the negligible collision, gravity is ignored and only contact impulses matter. Since the block slides immediately after impact, use kinetic friction during the impact: the tangential friction impulse has magnitude mu times the normal impulse and acts upslope. The normal impulse must remove the normal component of momentum, so J_N = m v cos(theta). Therefore the friction impulse reduces the downslope momentum by mu J_N = mu m v cos(theta). Apply impulse-momentum along the slope: m u = m v sin(theta) - mu m v cos(theta), giving u = v(sin(theta) - mu cos(theta)).

method.method_draft: Treat the event as a rough oblique impact with a fixed plane. Because the block does not bounce away and slides along the plane immediately after impact, take the normal coefficient of restitution effectively as e = 0, so the normal approach speed v cos(theta) is eliminated by the normal impulse. For rough impact with sliding, the change in tangential speed due to friction is mu times the lost normal approach speed, opposite the sliding direction. The incoming tangential speed down the plane is v sin(theta), so the outgoing tangential speed is u = v sin(theta) - mu v cos(theta).
method.CoT_raw: Treat the collision as a rough oblique impact with a fixed plane. Take the positive tangential direction to be down the ramp. Just before impact, the vertical speed v decomposes into a tangential component v sinθ down the plane and a normal approach component v cosθ into the plane. Since the block does not bounce away, use effective normal restitution e = 0, so the normal impulse removes the normal approach speed. Thus the normal impulse magnitude is J_n = m v cosθ. Because the block slides down the plane immediately after impact, kinetic friction acts up the plane during impact with impulse J_f = μ J_n = μ m v cosθ. This friction impulse reduces the tangential momentum: m u = m v sinθ - μ m v cosθ. Therefore u = v(sinθ - μ cosθ).
